appraisal_events.evidence: Nothing has more prestige for him than his mistress, 'infiniment plus de prestige que les Guermantes et tous les rois de la terre'; he plans to buy her a 30,000-franc necklace, secretly fears she stays only for his money, and the narrator notes he praises her only to seem more impressive to his friend ('je vis bien qu'il pensait tout le contraire').
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's analysis exposes Saint-Loup as wholly subordinated to his mistress emotionally and financially, anxious about whether she loves him, and even performing false modesty about her to bolster his own position in the narrator's eyes.

status_effects.explanation: Saint-Loup holds none of the emotional leverage in the relationship: he lavishes money and devotion on his mistress while fearing she does not love him and stays only for his wealth.
